title_tag: 父母留下的一屋子旧东西，年轻人到底要不要？美国一场93万亿美元的继承潮已经开始 —— 美国彭博社外刊讲解 第1181天
h1: 父母留下的一屋子旧东西，年轻人到底要不要？美国一场93万亿美元的继承潮已经开始
category: 美国彭博社外刊讲解 第1181天

headline.en_html: The Great Stuff Transfer Has a $750 Billion Golden Lining — In the coming avalanche of possessions being passed down from baby boomers to younger generations, jewelry is the bright spot.
headline.zh: “物品大转移”，藏着7500亿美元的金色里子——婴儿潮一代传给年轻人的这场财产雪崩里，珠宝是唯一的亮点。

notes.en: stuff (n.) means things in general, especially a large, unsorted collection of objects whose individual names are not worth listing
notes.zh: 东西，杂物（一堆杂七杂八、懒得一一叫出名字的物件）
notes.ctx: 作者刻意不用 assets 或 possessions，而用带嫌弃感的 stuff，把整篇文章的口吻从财经报道拉到家务事。
notes.ex1: The startup's warehouse was packed with stuff nobody had bothered to catalog for three years. 这家初创公司的仓库里塞满了三年来没人费心登记过的杂物。
notes.ex2: After the merger, employees spent a week clearing out the stuff left behind in the old offices. 合并之后，员工花了一周时间清理旧办公室里留下的那堆东西。

notes.en: transfer (v.) means to move someone or something from one place, person, or situation to another
notes.ctx: trans- 跨越 + -fer 带：未来二十年内，93 万亿美元资产及随之而来的实物，从婴儿潮一代与沉默的一代手中交到继承人手上。
notes.ex1: The bank completed the transfer of the client's assets within two working days. 银行在两个工作日内完成了客户资产的划转。
notes.ex2: She transferred the deed to her daughter long before the estate went to court. 早在遗产进入法庭程序之前，她就把房契过户给了女儿。

notes.en: lining (n.) means a layer of material that covers the inside surface of something, such as a coat or a bag
notes.ctx: 标题把“物品大转移”比作一件黑外套，而黄金就是这件外套的金色里子——价值 7500 亿美元。
notes.ex1: The jacket's worn lining betrayed how many winters it had survived. 外套磨损的里子暴露了它熬过多少个冬天。
notes.ex2: Doctors examined the lining of the patient's stomach for signs of inflammation. 医生检查了病人的胃壁，寻找炎症迹象。

notes.en: an avalanche means a mass of snow and ice sliding rapidly down a mountain; figuratively, a sudden overwhelming quantity of something
notes.zh: 雪崩；排山倒海涌来的一大批东西
notes.ctx: 作者用“雪崩”而不是“天降财富”，暗示这对继承人是灾难而非喜事。
notes.ex1: The product launch triggered an avalanche of customer complaints the support team could not absorb. 产品上线引发了客服团队根本消化不了的海量投诉。
notes.ex2: An avalanche of regulatory filings landed on the firm's desk the week before the deadline. 截止日期前一周，事务所桌上堆起了小山一样的监管文件。

notes.en: to pass something down means to give an object, tradition, or skill to a younger generation
notes.ctx: 全篇的主线动词：从副标题的“财产传向年轻人”，一路收束到最后一段那句 It was passed down to me。
notes.ex1: The family passed down the vineyard for five generations without ever selling a single plot. 这家人把葡萄园传了五代，一块地都没卖过。
notes.ex2: Craft techniques once passed down through apprenticeships are now taught in vocational schools. 过去靠师徒相传的手艺，如今在职业学校里教授。

notes.en: a bright spot means one encouraging or successful element within an otherwise disappointing situation
notes.ctx: 瓷器、银器、旧家具、棒球卡全线滞销的清单里，珠宝是唯一一样人人都愿意接手的东西。
notes.ex1: Overseas sales were the one bright spot in an otherwise dismal quarter. 在整体惨淡的一个季度里，海外销售是唯一的亮点。
notes.ex2: Rural clinics remained a rare bright spot in the country's strained health system. 在这个国家吃紧的医疗体系里，乡村诊所仍是少有的亮点。

paragraphs.en_html: 1. When Andrew Stinger’s mother, Nancy, died of cancer in 2024, her <mark class="voc">grief-stricken</mark> husband and sons began the journey of managing her <mark class="voc">estate</mark> in <mark class="voc">probate</mark> court — a process that would <mark class="voc">stretch</mark> almost two years. Then, in January 2025, Stinger’s father, Bill, died <mark class="voc">unexpectedly</mark>. And yet, there was one happy spot amid the <mark class="voc">heartbreak</mark>: the jewelry.
paragraphs.zh: 2024年，安德鲁·斯廷格的母亲南希因癌症离世。悲痛欲绝的丈夫和儿子们，就此踏上了在遗嘱认证法庭打理她遗产的漫漫长路——这一拖，就是将近两年。紧接着，2025年1月，斯廷格的父亲比尔又猝然离世。可即便在这样的伤痛里，仍有一处让人心头一暖的角落：珠宝。

notes.en: grief-stricken means overwhelmed by extreme sorrow, especially after a death
notes.ctx: stricken 是 strike 的过去分词“被击中”，这是英语里表示悲伤最重的一档词；作者不用 sad，暗示这家人是被打垮了。
notes.ex1: The grief-stricken widow could not bring herself to sort through her husband's study. 悲痛欲绝的遗孀始终无法动手整理丈夫的书房。
notes.ex2: Rescue workers comforted grief-stricken relatives waiting outside the collapsed building. 救援人员安抚着在坍塌楼房外等候的悲痛家属。

notes.en: estate (n.) means all the money, property, and possessions that a person owns at the time of their death
notes.zh: 遗产；去世时留下的全部财产
notes.ctx: 此处不是“庄园、房地产”，而是去世那一刻名下的全部财产——要先经法庭清点、还债，才谈得上分配。
notes.ex1: It took the executor eighteen months to settle an estate spread across three states. 遗嘱执行人花了十八个月，才处理完散布在三个州的遗产。
notes.ex2: Her estate was valued at just under two million dollars before taxes. 她的遗产在扣税前估值略低于两百万美元。

notes.en: probate (n.) means the official legal process by which a will is proved valid and a dead person's estate is administered
notes.ctx: 词根 prob- 就是“证明”：先证明遗嘱为真，才谈得上分家产——这也是遗产被拖近两年的制度原因。
notes.ex1: Assets held in a living trust pass to heirs without going through probate. 放在生前信托里的资产可以直接转给继承人，无需经过遗嘱认证。
notes.ex2: Probate fees consumed nearly eight percent of the family's inheritance. 遗嘱认证费用吃掉了这家人将近百分之八的遗产。

notes.en: stretch (v.) means to continue over a period of time, often longer than expected
notes.ctx: 本义是把东西在空间上抻长，用在时间上就带出“被拉长、令人疲惫”的味道，不是中性的“持续”。
notes.ex1: Negotiations stretched into a fourth week with no sign of a settlement. 谈判拖进了第四周，仍看不到和解的迹象。
notes.ex2: His tenure at the company stretched across four different CEOs. 他在公司任职的时间，横跨了四任首席执行官。

notes.en: unexpectedly means in a way that was not predicted or prepared for
notes.ctx: 与母亲因癌症去世“有心理准备”形成对照，父亲这一走是完全没有准备的第二次打击。
notes.ex1: The chief financial officer resigned unexpectedly two days before the earnings call. 首席财务官在财报电话会前两天突然辞职。
notes.ex2: Demand came in unexpectedly strong, forcing the factory onto a third shift. 需求意外强劲，迫使工厂加开第三班。

notes.en: heartbreak (n.) means overwhelming distress, especially caused by loss or the end of a relationship
notes.ctx: 一年内连失双亲的双重打击，也正是段末那个 happy spot（珠宝）的反面铺垫。
notes.ex1: The heartbreaking footage from the flood zone dominated the evening broadcast. 来自洪灾区的揪心画面占据了晚间新闻的大部分时段。
notes.ex2: She was heartbroken when the buyer withdrew the offer on her childhood home. 买家撤回对她童年老宅的报价时，她心碎不已。

paragraphs.en_html: 2. “There were <mark class="voc">pieces</mark> that my mom <mark class="voc">inherited</mark> from her mother that it <mark class="voc">made sense</mark> for my mom’s sisters to have, and to be able to pass down to their daughters,” Stinger says. “My mom’s <mark class="voc">engagement ring</mark> will go to her only granddaughter when she grows up. These things are part of our family <mark class="voc">lineage</mark>.”
paragraphs.zh: “有些首饰，是我妈从我外婆手里接下来的。这些东西由我几个姨妈收着，再往下传给她们的女儿，是最顺理成章的，”斯廷格说，“我妈那枚订婚戒指，等她唯一的孙女长大了，就归她。这些东西，本身就是我们家族血脉的一部分。”

notes.en: piece (n.) means a single item from a category, especially one item of jewelry, art, furniture, or music
notes.ctx: 珠宝行业的通用量词：不点明到底是戒指还是项链时，就用 a piece。
notes.ex1: The auction house priced the statement piece well above its estimate. 拍卖行给这件压轴首饰定的价远高于估价。
notes.ex2: Each piece in the collection carried the maker's mark on the clasp. 这套收藏里的每一件，搭扣上都带着制作者的印记。

notes.en: inherit (v.) means to receive money, property, or a title from someone after that person has died
notes.ctx: in- + herit（同源 heir / heritage），此处是一条从外婆到母亲、再到姨妈与她们女儿的完整母系传承链。
notes.ex1: He inherited a controlling stake in the business but had never run a company. 他继承了公司的控股权，却从未经营过企业。
notes.ex2: Inherited wealth accounts for a growing share of the country's top fortunes. 在这个国家最顶层的财富中，继承所得的占比正在上升。

notes.en: to make sense means to be reasonable, logical, or practical
notes.ctx: 斯廷格认为首饰由几位姨妈收着、再往下传给她们的女儿，是最顺理成章的安排。
notes.ex1: It makes sense to appraise the collection before dividing it among the siblings. 在兄弟姐妹之间分配之前，先给这批藏品估个价是明智的。
notes.ex2: Analysts could not make sense of the sudden change in guidance. 分析师们搞不懂业绩指引为何突然变化。

notes.en: an engagement ring means a ring given to mark a promise of marriage, typically set with a diamond
notes.ctx: 求婚时给出的那枚戒指，此处它要等一个还没长大的小姑娘。
notes.ex1: He spent three months' salary on an engagement ring, following a rule invented by an ad campaign. 他按一条广告造出来的规矩，花了三个月工资买订婚戒指。
notes.ex2: The couple chose a vintage engagement ring over anything newly made. 这对夫妇选了一枚古董订婚戒指，而不是全新的。

notes.en: lineage (n.) means the line of ancestors from whom a person or family is descended
notes.ctx: line + -age，把血脉想象成一条连续的线；他说首饰 are 血脉，而不只是 represent 血脉。
notes.ex1: The winery traces its lineage back to a single plot planted in 1748. 这家酒庄的血脉可以追溯到1748年栽下的一小块园地。
notes.ex2: He was of noble lineage but had spent his adult life avoiding the title. 他出身名门，成年后却一直回避这个头衔。

paragraphs.en_html: 3. In the next 20 years, some $93 trillion in assets in the US will be passed down from baby boomers and the Silent Generation to their <mark class="voc">heirs</mark>. Along with that will come a whole lot of physical items: the <mark class="voc">china</mark>, silver, coin and stamp collections, and millions and millions of baseball cards that <mark class="voc">make up</mark> <mark class="voc">what’s known as</mark> the Great Stuff Transfer.
paragraphs.zh: 未来二十年里，美国将有约93万亿美元的资产，从婴儿潮一代和沉默的一代手中，交到他们的继承人手上。而随着这笔钱一起涌来的，还有堆积如山的实物——成套的瓷器、银器，一册册的钱币和邮票，以及数也数不清的棒球卡。这些东西合在一起，就是人们所说的“物品大转移”。

notes.en: an heir means a person legally entitled to receive the property or title of someone who has died
notes.ctx: 法律上有权接手死者财产或头衔的人；此处指即将接住 93 万亿美元的那一代。
notes.ex1: The founder never named an heir, leaving the board to improvise after his death. 创始人从未指定继承人，他去世后董事会只能临时应对。
notes.ex2: As heir apparent, she had shadowed the chairman for nearly a decade. 作为内定接班人，她跟在董事长身边观摩了将近十年。

notes.en: china (n., lowercase) means plates, cups, and other tableware made of fine white porcelain
notes.ctx: 小写是瓷器（源自 China ware），与银器、钱币册、邮票册并列为二十世纪中产家庭的“体面四件套”。
notes.ex1: The couple registered for bone china they would use exactly twice a year. 这对新人登记了一套骨瓷，而他们一年只会用它两次。
notes.ex2: Her grandmother's china sat untouched in the cabinet for three decades. 她祖母的那套瓷器在柜子里原封不动放了三十年。

notes.en: to make up means to combine to form a whole; also to invent, to reconcile, or to compensate
notes.ctx: 此处是“合起来构成”：瓷器、银器、钱币、邮票、棒球卡凑成了所谓 the Great Stuff Transfer。
notes.ex1: Women make up just under half of the firm's engineering staff. 女性占这家公司工程团队的将近一半。
notes.ex2: He made up for the delay by covering the entire shipping cost. 他承担了全部运费，以弥补延误。

notes.en: what is known as means what people commonly call or refer to as
notes.ctx: 用来引出 the Great Stuff Transfer 这个生造术语——它是在戏仿既有的财经术语 the Great Wealth Transfer。
notes.ex1: Economists call it what's known as a liquidity trap, where rate cuts stop working. 经济学家称之为流动性陷阱，在这种情况下降息失去作用。
notes.ex2: The practice is commonly known as quiet quitting among younger employees. 这种做法在年轻员工中通常被称为“安静离职”。

paragraphs.en_html: 4. Jewelry is the rare <mark class="voc">exception</mark>. The reasons are both obvious and <mark class="voc">intimate</mark>: To begin with, silver, gold, platinum and gemstones have material value. With gold prices climbing back toward their January high (when the <mark class="voc">spot price</mark> was $5,589.38 per ounce, five times what it was 10 years earlier) and silver on a similar <mark class="voc">trajectory</mark>, it’s a good time to <mark class="voc">come into</mark> some precious metal. According to a 2026 report from the jewelry tracking startup Unvault Inc., the average US household is <mark class="voc">sitting on</mark> $5,700 in <mark class="voc">unappraised</mark> gold jewelry, with roughly $750 billion in gold weight in drawers across the country. Add to that silver, platinum and pieces with artistic <mark class="voc">merit</mark> that can <mark class="voc">command</mark> high <mark class="voc">premiums</mark>.
paragraphs.zh: 珠宝是其中罕见的例外。理由既摆在明面上，也藏在心里头。首先，白银、黄金、铂金和宝石，本身就是有料的——它们的价值是实打实的材料价值。眼下金价正一路爬回1月份的高位（当时现货价每盎司5589.38美元，是十年前的整整五倍），白银也走着同样的上行轨迹，此时此刻继承到一点贵金属，运气实在不错。珠宝估值平台Unvault 2026年的一份报告显示，美国家庭平均坐拥价值5700美元、却从未估过价的金饰——全国上下的抽屉里，按黄金重量算，大约躺着7500亿美元。这还没算上白银、铂金，以及那些凭艺术价值就能卖出高溢价的作品。

notes.en: an exception means a person or thing that is not included in a general rule or statement
notes.ctx: 在艺术品、旧家具、棒球卡全线滞销的清单里，珠宝是唯一人人愿意接手的，作者还加了 rare 强调其难得。
notes.ex1: Every division missed its target, with the exception of logistics. 除物流部门外，每个事业部都没完成指标。
notes.ex2: The committee made an exception for applicants affected by the border closure. 委员会为受边境关闭影响的申请者破了例。

notes.en: intimate (adj.) means closely personal and private, involving a very close connection
notes.ctx: 来自拉丁语 intimus“最深处的”；obvious 那一半讲钱，intimate 那一半讲情感，文章最终落在后者。
notes.ex1: The restaurant traded its cavernous dining room for a more intimate space upstairs. 这家餐厅放弃了空旷的大厅，换成楼上更私密的空间。
notes.ex2: She had intimate knowledge of the negotiation, having drafted every clause. 她对这场谈判了如指掌，每一条款都是她起草的。

notes.en: the spot price means the current market price at which an asset can be bought or sold for immediate delivery
notes.ctx: 当场成交的价，与期货价相对：1 月每盎司 5589.38 美元，是十年前约 1118 美元的整整五倍。
notes.ex1: The spot price of copper jumped four percent after the mine suspended operations. 矿场停产后，铜的现货价格跳涨了百分之四。
notes.ex2: Refiners hedge in the futures market rather than buying at the spot price. 炼厂在期货市场对冲，而不是按现货价采购。

notes.en: a trajectory means the curved path of a moving object, or the general direction in which something develops
notes.ctx: 物理弹道那条弧线，比 trend 更强调“已经射出去，方向不会变”。
notes.ex1: The company has been on an upward trajectory since it abandoned hardware. 自从放弃硬件业务，这家公司一直走在上行轨道上。
notes.ex2: A single regulatory ruling altered the trajectory of the entire sector. 一纸监管裁定改变了整个行业的走向。

notes.en: to come into something means to inherit or unexpectedly receive money or property
notes.zh: 继承到，意外获得一笔财产
notes.ctx: 这里不是“入行投资贵金属”，而是“此时此刻继承到一点贵金属”；整句方向若译反，意思完全相反。
notes.ex1: He came into a modest fortune just as the housing market peaked. 他继承到一笔不小的财产时，正赶上楼市见顶。
notes.ex2: She came into her grandmother's property at twenty-three and sold it within a year. 她二十三岁继承了祖母的房产，一年内就卖掉了。

notes.en: to sit on something means to possess something valuable without using, selling, or acting on it
notes.ctx: 坐在上面却不动：家里明明有价值 5700 美元的金饰，却从没估过价，也从没想过它值多少。
notes.ex1: The family was sitting on a gold mine and had no idea until the appraiser arrived. 在估价师上门之前，这家人根本不知道自己坐拥一座金矿。
notes.ex2: Corporations are sitting on record cash piles rather than investing. 企业手握创纪录的现金，却按兵不投。

notes.en: appraise (v.) means to assess the monetary value or quality of something in an official way
notes.ctx: unappraised 即“从未经专业估价”；也正因为没估过价，多数人也没给这些金饰上保险。
notes.ex1: The necklace was appraised at four times what the owner had assumed. 这条项链的估价是物主原以为的四倍。
notes.ex2: Annual performance appraisals were replaced with quarterly check-ins. 年度绩效考核被季度沟通所取代。

notes.en: merit (n.) means the quality of being good, valuable, or deserving of praise
notes.ctx: artistic merit 指金属重量之外，设计与工艺本身带来的那部分价值。
notes.ex1: The proposal has merit, though the timeline is unrealistic. 这个提案有可取之处，只是时间表不现实。
notes.ex2: Applications are judged strictly on merit, without regard to connections. 申请一律按能力评判，不看人脉。

notes.en: command (v.) means to deserve and receive something, such as a high price or respect, because of one's quality or standing
notes.zh: （凭实力）卖得出某个价，博得（尊重）
notes.ctx: 不是“命令”，而是主动语态下的“能要到这个价”，语感远强于被动的 be sold for。
notes.ex1: Vintage watches from that decade still command a premium at auction. 那十年出产的古董表在拍卖会上依然能卖出溢价。
notes.ex2: She commands respect in the room without ever raising her voice. 她从不提高嗓门，却能让全场心悦诚服。

notes.en: a premium means an amount paid above the normal or basic price
notes.ctx: 高于金属本身价格的溢价；也是后文 Unvault 抽 10%–20% 手续费那一段的对照概念。
notes.ex1: Buyers pay a steep premium for signed pieces from a recognizable maison. 对于出自知名珠宝世家、带签名的作品，买家愿意付高额溢价。
notes.ex2: Office space near the station is at a premium during the expansion. 扩建期间，车站附近的办公空间非常紧俏。

paragraphs.en_html: 5. Unlike art, old furniture or Dickens houses, the <mark class="voc">infrastructure</mark> for <mark class="voc">offloading</mark> jewelry at almost any <mark class="voc">price point</mark> is expansive and well established. From estate-sale specialists, <mark class="voc">pawnshops</mark> and local jewelers to high-end <mark class="voc">auction</mark> houses to eBay and the RealReal, there are options for <mark class="voc">pretty much</mark> everything you could inherit.
paragraphs.zh: 跟艺术品、老家具或者那些狄更斯圣诞小屋不同，珠宝变现的那一整套体系，无论哪个价位，都既宽且熟。从上门清点遗物的专员、街角当铺、本地珠宝行，到高端拍卖行，再到eBay和The RealReal——你可能继承到的几乎任何东西，都能找到接盘的地方。

notes.en: infrastructure (n.) means the basic systems and facilities that allow an organization, market, or country to function
notes.zh: 基础设施；支撑一件事运转的整套体系
notes.ctx: 不限于水泥钢筋，此处指从遗产清仓专员、当铺到拍卖行的整条变现渠道链，正是艺术品与旧家具所缺的。
notes.ex1: The country has the gold reserves but lacks the financial infrastructure to mobilize them. 这个国家有黄金储备，却缺少把它调动起来的金融基础设施。
notes.ex2: Payments moved online long before the regulatory infrastructure caught up. 支付早已线上化，监管体系却迟迟没跟上。

notes.en: offload (v.) means to get rid of something unwanted by passing it on to someone else
notes.ctx: 不用中性的 sell，而用带“想赶紧弄走”意味的 offload，一个词点破继承在很多人眼里是负担而非财富。
notes.ex1: The fund quietly offloaded its stake over six weeks to avoid moving the price. 该基金在六周内悄悄减持，以免影响股价。
notes.ex2: Retailers offloaded unsold inventory at a fraction of the original price. 零售商以原价的零头甩卖了滞销库存。

notes.en: a price point means the particular price level at which a product is offered within a range
notes.ctx: 价格区间上的一个点：几十块的镀金耳环和几十万的钻石项链，各有各的出口，这才是“基础设施成熟”的真意。
notes.ex1: The brand launched a lower price point to reach first-time buyers. 该品牌推出了一个更低的价位，以吸引首次购买的消费者。
notes.ex2: Competing across every price point stretched the company's supply chain thin. 在每个价位上都参与竞争，把公司的供应链拉得过薄。

notes.en: a pawnshop means a shop that lends money in exchange for objects left as security
notes.ctx: 在美国常与发薪日贷款店同街，带着“经济困境”的社会标签，正是很多女性打死不肯踏进去的那种店。
notes.ex1: He pawned his camera twice that winter and redeemed it both times. 那年冬天他两次典当相机，又两次赎了回来。
notes.ex2: She was a pawn in a corporate fight she had never been told about. 她成了一场自己毫不知情的公司斗争中的一颗棋子。

notes.en: an auction means a public sale in which goods are sold to the highest bidder
notes.ctx: 来自拉丁语 augere“不断增加”——拍卖的本质就是价格一轮轮往上加；此处是变现链条的高端一环。
notes.ex1: The brooch went to auction with no reserve and tripled its estimate. 这枚胸针以无底价上拍，成交价是估价的三倍。
notes.ex2: Two smaller regional auction houses handled the remainder of the estate. 遗产的其余部分由两家规模较小的地方拍卖行处理。

notes.en: pretty much means almost completely; more or less
notes.ctx: 口语里的“基本上、差不多”：不管你继承到什么，几乎都能找到出路。
notes.ex1: The integration is pretty much finished apart from the payroll system. 除了薪酬系统，整合基本上已经完成。
notes.ex2: Both proposals are pretty much the same once you strip out the branding. 去掉包装之后，这两份提案基本上是一回事。
